    Our craft

    The part you never see is the part we obsess over.

    Anyone can hang a TV. We build the system behind it — racked, labeled, ventilated and documented — so it runs cool, sounds right, and can be serviced in minutes, not hours.

    • 01

      Planned before a single hole

      Speaker placement, viewing angles, wiring paths and network coverage are designed up front — around your room and how you live in it.

    • 02

      Rack-built & labeled

      Every cable loomed, strapped and labeled. If anything ever needs attention, the next visit is fast — whoever's on it.

    • 03

      Calibrated, then walked through

      Picture and sound tuned to the room, controls simplified to one remote — and we stay until you're comfortable running it.

    How it works

    From first call to movie night in four steps

    1

    Talk & design

    Tell Kyle or Steve what you want the room to do. We'll talk through gear, placement and budget — honestly, including what you don't need.

    2

    Clear, itemized quote

    You get a written quote with equipment and labor spelled out — no vague allowances, no surprises after the walls are open.

    3

    Install & calibrate

    Clean, careful installation: wiring hidden, rack labeled, picture and sound calibrated to your room and seating.

    4

    Walkthrough & support

    We program one simple control, walk you through it in person, and stay reachable when questions come up later.

      For Kyle — the thinking

      What I changed, and why

      I kept everything true about the current phetv.com — the headline, the 5.0 rating, the troubleshooter, the family story — and rebuilt the structure around how people actually hire an integrator.

      A. One job per screen

      The current homepage asks visitors to do five things at once. Here the hero has one promise (“Every detail”), one primary action (Request a quote) and the rating as proof — everything else lives further down, in order.

      B. Services in ten seconds

      Six services, plain-language outcomes, and tags for the specifics (Sonos, Atmos, hidden wires). A homeowner in Surprise should be able to find “my ceiling speakers don't work” without knowing AV vocabulary.

      C. Proof over adjectives

      Your rack photo does more selling than any paragraph — so craftsmanship gets a full section, and the Google rating appears in the hero, mid-page, and next to the quote form. Trust is placed where the decision happens.

      D. The showroom, simplified

      I loved the interactive room concept on the current site, so I kept it — but as one tap-to-switch panel instead of a separate experience. Same delight, zero extra pages to maintain.

      E. Help that earns calls

      The troubleshooter stays, promoted to the homepage. It filters out the five-minute fixes, builds goodwill, and the people who still call are warmer, better-qualified leads.

      F. Built for thumbs

      Most quote requests will start on a phone, so mobile gets a permanent Call / Get a quote bar, tap targets stay large, and the form is four fields. On the real build this form posts to Jobber exactly like today.

      Imagery: the living-room hero and equipment-rack photos are from your current site; the theater, evening and patio photos are stand-ins to show layout and would be swapped for your own project photos before launch.
